record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Find an Einstein-Yang-Mills analogue of the Majumdar-Papetrou superposition of extremal Reissner-Nordstrom solutions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. The Majumdar–Papapetrou family of solutions to the source-free Einstein–Maxwell equations on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold consists of static metrics of the form
  g = -U(x)^{-2} dt^2 + U(x)^2 (dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2),
together with electromagnetic potential A = U(x)^{-1} dt, where U: R^3 \ {p_1,...,p_N} -> (0,∞) is any positive harmonic function on Euclidean R^3 with isolated singularities at points p_1,...,p_N. After analytic extension, each singularity p_k becomes a degenerate (extremal) Killing horizon, so the solution describes an arbitrary number of extremal Reissner–Nordström black holes held in static equilibrium by the exact balance of their gravitational attraction and electrostatic repulsion. The defining feature is that the linearity of the harmonic equation for U allows arbitrary superposition of single-black-hole solutions.

Problem. Construct a non-Abelian Einstein–Yang–Mills analogue of this Majumdar–Papapetrou superposition. More precisely: for a compact non-Abelian gauge group G (e.g. SU(2)), find static, asymptotically flat solutions of the coupled Einstein–Yang–Mills equations on R x (R^3 \ {p_1,...,p_N}) which (i) describe an equilibrium configuration of N ≥ 2 extremal black-hole-type horizons located at prescribed points p_1,...,p_N in R^3, with (ii) the metric and Yang–Mills connection determined by a superposition principle reducing the problem to a (possibly non-linear) elliptic system on R^3 with isolated singularities, and which (iii) reduces to the Majumdar–Papapetrou solution upon restriction of the gauge field to an Abelian subgroup. Alternatively, prove that no such Einstein–Yang–Mills multi-black-hole equilibrium analogue of Majumdar–Papapetrou exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches reveal extensive work on Majumdar–Papapetrou solutions in Einstein–Maxwell theory and on single-horizon Einstein–Yang–Mills black holes (e.g., Smoller–Wasserman–Yau existence theorems, Wu–Yang ansatz solutions, Bogomol'nyi-type equations in Einstein–Yang–Mills–Higgs), as well as recent spinning generalizations of Majumdar–Papapetrou by Teo–Wan in Einstein–Maxwell. However, no construction of a genuine non-Abelian Einstein–Yang–Mills multi-black-hole equilibrium analogue of the Majumdar–Papapetrou superposition was found, nor a no-go theorem ruling it out. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Existence of Black Hole Solutions for the Einstein-Yang/Mills Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Black hole solutions to the Einstein-Yang-Mills equations with gauge group SU(2) exist for any event horizon.
status_evidence.claim: Single-horizon EYM black holes are known, but no multi-black-hole MP analogue is reported.

status_evidence.title: Spinning generalizations of Majumdar-Papapetrou multi-black hole spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: A generalization of the Majumdar-Papapetrou multi-black hole spacetime describing charged and spinning (extremal) balanced black holes in asymptotically flat spacetime was recently constructed by Teo and Wan.
status_evidence.claim: Recent generalizations of MP remain within Einstein–Maxwell, not Einstein–Yang–Mills.

status_evidence.title: Bogomol'nyi equations in the Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs system
status_evidence.snippet: Bogomol'nyi equations in the Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs system
status_evidence.claim: BPS-type equilibrium configurations exist in EYM-Higgs but a pure EYM Majumdar–Papapetrou analogue is not established.
